_comment: Expected failures for scripts/check_fresh_clone.sh. AN ENTRY HERE MEANS THE ASSERTION DOES NOT HOLD AND IS KNOWN NOT TO HOLD. It is never a pass and it never makes the absolute run green: `bash scripts/check_fresh_clone.sh` with no arguments re-runs a pinned assertion and still exits 1 on it. A pin buys exactly one thing, and it is the thing this repo has been burned by three times: a review does not reject a worker for debt the worker inherited. Only the two assertions named in PINNABLE, which lives in check_fresh_clone.sh's CODE and not here, may appear; any other key exits 2. A pinned assertion that starts PASSING is a failure (PIN STALE) and a pinned assertion that fails for a reason its `signature` does not match is a failure (PIN MISMATCH), so a pin cannot outlive its problem and cannot mute an area. Adding an entry grows this dict, which check_ratchets_not_loosened.py reads as a loosened ratchet and rejects inside a review.
_measured: 2026-09-02: both pinned assertions were re-measured by running it and BOTH NOW HOLD, so both pins are gone and both assertions gate. The frontend half was fixed by making apps/registry.tsx discover apps with import.meta.glob instead of naming their pages in literal import() specifiers: with the app source deleted the glob matches nothing and tsc -b is clean, where before it gave 20x TS2307. The backend half was two separate things -- services/app_registry.py no longer importing every app's modules, and check_no_app_names.py no longer misclassifying the platform module routes/notes_all.py as app source, which is what the fresh clone was deleting out from under `import main`. Empty dict below is the point: no assertion here is excused.
